reasons: Covers allowed events, privacy filtering and the API with clear expectations.
Uses a database reset and a controlled session.

terms.meaning: a stand-in for a real part of the app, used so a test can control it.
key performance indicator, a headline number used to judge the product.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Mocked session and setup
sections.what: Resets the database and replaces the real sign-in check with a variable the test controls.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets each test act as any user without a real sign-in.
sections.watch_out: The mock applies to the whole file.

sections.name: analytics events
sections.title: Analytics event rules
sections.what: Checks browser events are restricted, the event list is correct, valid events are stored for users or anonymously, personal fields and out-of-range values are rejected, and the API behaves correctly.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the key numbers server-side and personal data out of analytics.
sections.watch_out: The event list test fails by design when a new event is added without updating the spec.

summary: Tests the analytics system: browsers cannot send server-only events, only listed event names are accepted, extra personal fields are rejected, and the events API works.
purpose: Protects the trustworthiness of the app's usage numbers and keeps personal data out of them.
why: Likely reason: key business numbers must come from the server, and analytics must not collect personal details.
how: Mocks the auth module so the test can set the current user. Resets the database. Checks that browser-sent events for locked calls, graded calls and review views are rejected. Checks the event list matches the spec. Stores a valid event with a user, and an anonymous event with none. Rejects an email field and an out-of-range confidence value. Checks the events API returns 201 for a valid name and 400 for an unknown one.
inputs: Test data and the mocked session user.
outputs: A pass or fail result for each test.
risks: The mock replaces the real auth module for the whole file. The event list must be updated whenever the spec changes.
debug: If the event list fails, compare it with the spec. If the API returns the wrong status, check the events route's validation.
